account: Researchers at the International Center of Insect Physiology and Ecology (icipe) used MaxEnt to predict desert locust breeding regions. The paper describes MaxEnt as a machine learning algorithm. Co-authors came from the Desert Locust Control Organization for Eastern Africa (DLCO-EA), Kenya's Plant Protection Services and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), including Keith Cressman of FAO. The authors accessed 9,134 records from FAO and the Moroccan anti-locust center. They used 5,406 breeding sites from Morocco (367), Mauritania (2,661) and Saudi Arabia (1,703). The records date from 1985 to 2020. The authors used 70% of the records for training and 30% for testing. They measured accuracy as the area under the curve (AUC). Of the three country models, the Mauritania model had the highest mean AUC (0.887), followed by Saudi Arabia (0.884) and Morocco (0.820). The Morocco model, projected to Mauritanian and Saudi sites that it had not used, gave a mean predicted suitability of 0.85 at the Mauritanian sites and 0.84 at the Saudi sites. The authors projected the models to potential oviposition and breeding areas in Kenya, Uganda, South Sudan and Sudan. They thank DLCO-EA and Kenya's Ministry of Agriculture for field data. The paper, published on 20 July 2020, does not report use of the predictions in control operations. Among 30 papers indexed in Europe PMC that cite the study by 29 October 2026, none reports that FAO, DLCO-EA or national teams used the maps.
